scope: Typical operating values visible to a generic SAE J1979 mode-01 reader. Public sources only (BMW technical training manuals publicly mirrored on archive.org / bmwtechinfo, NHTSA-published BMW SIs, BMW press, forums, tuner docs). Numbers are plausibility windows, not pass/fail limits.

generic_notes.units: OBD PID 0x0B MAP is absolute kPa (max 255). PID 0x23 fuel rail gauge pressure in kPa x10 (max 655,350 kPa) is needed for 350 bar GDI; PID 0x22 range is too small. PID 0x10 MAF in g/s; BMW tools show kg/h (1 g/s = 3.6 kg/h).
generic_notes.valvetronic_map: On Valvetronic engines low idle vacuum is NORMAL; do not flag 'high MAP at idle' as a vacuum leak. Compare MAP to BARO (PID 0x33).
omitted: idle_rpm warm/cold (no public BMW figure or reliable logs found for any listed engine)
generic fuel-trim % window (no BMW public figure)

engines.family: BMW modular B-series petrol (Bx8: B38/B46/B48 share design)
engines.injection: gasoline direct injection (solenoid, central), single turbo, electric wastegate
engines.variants_note: Your F40 118i = B38A15M1 (TU generation). Gen-1 (B38A15M0, F48/F45 2014-2018) numbers below come from the BMW B46/B38 training manual.

valvetronic.note: Valve gear table in BMW 'B46 Engine' manual (covers B38+B46 as 'Bx8'): Double VANOS + Valvetronic (4th gen). unixnerd confirms 'all the engines have Valvetronic and double VANOS'. Note: Wikipedia B38 article does not mention Valvetronic.

map_idle.note: Valvetronic (throttle-free load control): the throttle stays nearly open and is only slightly closed to create a small vacuum for crankcase ventilation/purge. Expect MAP at warm idle close to barometric pressure (well above the ~30-40 kPa of a throttled engine). No published numeric MAP value found -> app should compare MAP with BARO (PID 0x33) instead of a fixed kPa.

maf_idle.note: No BMW-published idle MAF. Diagnostic rule of thumb: warm-idle MAF in g/s ~ displacement in litres (x1-2), varies with A/C and electrical load. Use only as a coarse plausibility window; judge together with fuel trims.

fuel_rail_pressure_max_gen1.note: Gen-1 Bx8 (B38/B46): 'maximum pressure in the rail is 200 bar'; HP pump relief valve opens at 245 bar.

fuel_rail_pressure_max_tu.note: B-series petrol update announced 2016 (TU engines, incl. B38A15M1 in F40) raised injection pressure to up to 350 bar. Only press/secondary sources; not confirmed per engine code. SAE J1979 PID 0x23 (rail gauge) max 655,350 kPa covers this.

fuel_low_pressure.note: Electric fuel pump supply ~5 bar (i8 B38 manual: 'about 5 bar, regulated via pressure-limiting valve'); Bx8 manual: max low pressure 6.5 bar (emergency mode with quantity control valve unpowered).

fuel_rail_pressure_idle.note: Not published. DME sets rail pressure from load/speed map; N55 manual states 200 bar is only needed at high load/low rpm, so idle is far below max. Compare 'actual' vs commanded rather than a fixed number.

coolant_temp_warm.note: Bx8 uses a DME map-controlled thermostat (confirmed) but the manual gives no targets. Range taken by analogy from N20 map-thermostat targets (80 high-load ... 109 economy). Expect 95-109 °C on light-load driving; values >112-115 °C warrant a look.

boost_max.note: Only published figure is for the i8 B38K15T0 ('charging pressure of up to 1.5 bar'); manual doesn't say gauge or absolute. Not representative for 118i (lower output). OBD PID 0x0B MAP is absolute and capped at 255 kPa.

fuel_trim_notes.note: BMW SI B11 07 17 (B38T/B46O in F48 X1, i8): fault 118002 'mixture too rich' in winter / short trips - fuel-laden crankcase vapours from cold oil enter the intake; DME mixture adaptation (multiplicative factor, NOT OBD STFT/LTFT %) at warm idle 'significantly below 1.0' = rich. Fix per BMW: oil change + DME software. Expect negative trims on short-trip cars in winter.
